main_topics.reason: The user repeatedly asked whether 2.4 g or 4.8 g was right and whether their prescription was too low.
The user said they were diagnosed about a month ago and were starting mesalamine for ulcerative colitis.
The user described their symptoms as moderate when explaining their concern about the prescribed dose.
The user asked why formulation mattered and described their medicine as twice-daily granule sachets.
The user asked whether to take the sachets with food in one turn.
The user asked how long it would take to know whether mesalamine was working.

output.summary: The user wanted to know whether their prescribed mesalamine dose of 1.2 g twice daily was appropriate after the assistant initially gave 4.8 g/day as a typical dose. The assistant corrected itself, explained that dose depends on formulation and treatment context, and answered questions about sachets, food, and onset; the user said they felt better and thanked it for clarifying.
